newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks drop 2.7pct in profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks drop 2.7pct in profit taking.

text.p: Greek stocks were trading 2.7 percent lower in mid-session with construction and bank shares down 4.54 and 3.90 percent respectively in profit taking, analysts said.
Decliners were leading gainers 165 to 28 with the general share index at 1,266.08.

"Investors are liquidating their positions after enjoying high capital gains in the last two months. They are cautious about the bourse's rise in the short term," said George Dimitriou, an analyst at Ergasias Securities.
He added that investors were waiting to see further developments in basic economic figures, such as inflation and interest rates, before repositioning.
Another investment manager said it was natural for the bourse to drop on Wednesday after its strong rise in February.
"There is profit taking because many investors gained a lot of money in the first two months of the year," said George Kartalis, investment manager at Alico Eurobank.
He added that the crisis in neighbouring Albania had not as yet influenced the Greek bourse.
"We would be in for trouble only if we were faced with waves of refugees trying to enter the country or if FYROM (Macedonia) became involved in the crisis," he said.
